name: Rooms
tagline: Places that do not exist, running live. Every entry here ships zero video.
_note: There is not one video file in this channel. Each entry is a script that loads the real room in an iframe and drives it on a clock. Paths resolve against THIS file's URL, so ../../misty-canoe.html is the app sitting next door in the same repo. Every selector below was read out of the live DOM in headless Chromium before it was written down — see rappvision/VERIFY.md.

videos.title: Nine rooms that don't exist — a seven-minute tour with no video file
videos.description:
An ambient channel that ships no video.

Every room below is a single HTML file — 68 to 78 KB, Three.js and Web Audio, no build step, no server. The usual way to publish this tour would be to render it to 4K and upload roughly a gigabyte. Instead this entry is a few kilobytes of JSON: the player opens each real room in an iframe and replays the recorded gestures against a clock.

Which means the thing you are looking at is not footage. Pause anywhere and the room keeps running, because it was never a recording — drag to look around, walk off the path, stay in the cave after the tour has moved on.

Nine rooms, in order: a canoe on a still lake at dawn; the floor of a rainforest looking up; a cabin under the aurora at 76° north; a glass elevator at dusk; a 1953 music box; a tea room; a library at fourteen minutes past midnight; an empty concert hall; and a cave lit only by larvae.

videos.title: Three kinds of rain, and none of them are a video
videos.description:
Rain on glass, rain through a canopy, rain on neon.

The conservatory is Victorian and the storm is real weather — press L and lightning arrives on your schedule, not on the timeline's. The forest is the Olympic Peninsula in October, looking straight up. The last one is a street that only exists at night.

The point of putting these three side by side: a rain video is the same rain every time you play it. These are simulations, so the drops fall somewhere different on every run, and if you pause and hold the pointer still the sound keeps going.

videos.title: Ten minutes on a still lake — one room, no cuts, no video
videos.description:
Slow TV, without the TV part.

One room for ten unbroken minutes: a cedar canoe on glass-still water in Algonquin Park, before the world wakes. The script does almost nothing — a paddle stroke every minute or so, a slow look at the far shore, and then it leaves you alone.

That is deliberate. This is the entry to prove the format is not a demo reel: a live channel can be boring on purpose, and it costs the same few kilobytes as a busy one. There is no encoder in this pipeline, so there is no bitrate to pay for the empty parts.

Headphones. The loon is worth it.
